reason: E1 and E2 show Cr segregation to dislocations in N-added austenitic steels via an I-S mechanism, but this requires N and is not demonstrated for cold-worked plus annealed 316L without N. E3 states Cr and Mo are important for passive films but provides no evidence linking defect-induced segregation to improved corrosion resistance. The key mechanistic steps from cold work to segregation to passive film enhancement are therefore largely unsupported by the cited evidence.
premises: Cold work introduces dislocations that act as fast diffusion paths for Cr
Low-temperature annealing drives Cr segregation to dislocations and grain boundaries
Cr segregation at defects promotes nucleation and stabilization of a passive oxide film
Enhanced passive film improves corrosion resistance (lower current density, higher pitting potential)
Mo contributes to maintaining the passive film
